notes.title: How your feedback is shaping Earthless
notes.content:
Hello, Captains!

For the small team working on Earthless here at Blackbird Interactive, October’s Steam Next Fest was nothing short of incredible. And we have you to thank for that!

Thousands of you downloaded and played the Earthless demo during Next Fest. Many of you even took time to give us invaluable feedback via our Steam Forums, [url=https://discord.gg/mJu5ef6Y9E]official Discord[/url], and on [url=https://twitter.com/earthlessgame]social media[/url]. And that feedback has not only strengthened our conviction that Earthless is an exciting blend of genres we love. It also helped us feel confident in what we can improve ahead of our 2024 Early Access launch. So thank you so much to everyone who took the time to share their thoughts on the demo.

[b]Today, I wanted to debrief on Next Fest and share how your feedback is shaping Earthless — especially as it relates to three key areas: difficulty, user interface, and the intro experience. [/b]

Let’s get to it, Captain!

[i]Pssst! If you're not on the [url=https://discord.gg/mJu5ef6Y9E][b]official Earthless Discord[/b][/url], you're missing out! Chat with the devs and other captains directly, be the first to know about major updates, and get a cool behind-the-scenes window into development![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/4ab21227be0b099ca01228bec38d5ebe5364fed3.png[/img]
[i]Above: A sneak peek at a new work-in-progress Lusk unit that creates an aura that buffs nearby units.[/i]

[h1]White-knuckle tactics[/h1]

[b]TL;DR: Demo difficulty was a tad too easy, the full game will be better balanced and provide a meatier challenge.[/b]

One thing we heard from many players is that the demo is simply too easy. We agree! Because Steam Next Fest is essentially a Farmer’s Market for video games, we wanted to ensure the game was fun for everyone — even those who never played a deckbuilder before. But, in retrospect, we might’ve played it a bit too safe.

Digging deeper, there’s two elements to consider: The first is that the demo only represents the first of three Star Maps planned for Early Access launch (even more will be added over time). Naturally, the first Star Map is meant to be on the easier side. Difficulty will scale up as you explore deeper into the cosmos and collect more powerful cards and Artifacts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/8ebf40b088fd283923eca455f46d7d99d09afb5a.jpg[/img]
[i]Above: Later Star Maps will add unique zones. Here's a mockup of an ice field that the team is currently working on.[/i]

But the second element at play here is that, simply, the combat encounters in the first Star Map are too easy. There’s a lot of variables at play — everything from the starting deck for each ship class to balance and power of individual cards or play styles. We’re also looking at factors like enemy HP, attack damage, and how many appear during encounters. Expect all of that to change as we get closer to Early Access (and in any future play tests we may do before then!).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/0f1300f406bc00408509808404e13af27a2adeda.gif[/img]
[i]Above: We're already hard at work on making the Crafting & Upgrades Console more intuitive (and way cooler).[/i]

[h1]Improving the user interface[/h1]

[b]TL;DR: The UI, especially in combat, will be improved over time to make it easier to check status effects, predict enemy attacks and movement, and more.[/b]

Earthless’ user interface is one of our favorite aspects of the whole game. We’ve gone to great lengths to build a diegetic command console that feels like you’re using an actual computer to give combat commands or check the status of your crew. But Earthless is a complex roguelike that needs to communicate a lot of information to players, and we’ve received plenty of comments identifying areas that need improvement.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/f80266f5758b89edb61739129fd4ce78fdbebf6d.gif[/img]
[i]Above: More colorful and dynamic tile effects will help you better understand the terrain of the battlefield and what's happening.[/i]

There’s almost too much to cover in just one blog post, so let me give you a quick overview of what we’re looking into:
[list]
[*] Change the position of important buttons on the command console, like your Ship Ability, so that it’s more intuitive (a lot of people reported forgetting their Ship Ability even existed!).
[*] Refactor how we display important intel like status effects so they’re easier to understand at a glance.
[*] Create a physical command console button for the Predictive AI module that shows you what enemies will do on their next turn. ([b]If you didn’t know this existed, you’re not alone! Try pressing TAB next time you’re in combat![/b])
[*] Clean up the Predictive AI interface so it’s easier to tell what will happen during the next turn, especially in bigger fights where it can get especially confusing.
[*] Adjust how the Crafting, Recycling, and Upgrading interface works to make it more intuitive
[*] Improve the readability of text across all consoles while still retaining that nostalgic CRT goodness.
[/list]
By and large these UI fixes will help you access the information you need to make better decisions in combat and elsewhere. This work is all just getting started, but I can’t wait to share updates and progress with you in the new year.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/2533aee74a9793393abf3b4bda7d9b027ca83278.png[/img]
[i]Above: New zones each have a distinctive look and modifiers that'll affect combat in fascinating ways.[/i]

[h1]On your maiden voyage…[/h1]

[b]TL;DR: The tutorial and game intro will be overhauled at some point in Early Access and replaced with a version that is much more immersive, comprehensive, and intuitive. [/b]

There’s a very thin line to walk when you’re making a demo for a game that is still in active development like Earthless. Even though demos are just a small slice of the full game, so many features and assets (like enemy models, music, or card art) are in varying stages of “completeness.” We wanted to show as much as we could, but also had to make hard choices about what to cut because it simply wasn’t ready.

One of those hard choices involved the “first-time user experience” — everything from the cinematic that plays when you first start the game to the tutorials that teach you how to command your crew or navigate intense combat encounters.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/5a685be21307cb2476dd8c6e37deaa3e828c1452.jpg[/img]
[i]Above: Taking on combat encounters in the Solar zone could wreck havoc on your Heat level.[/i]

By the time Earthless leaves Early Access, we want to have a more interactive intro and tutorial that better equips you with all the information you need to survive your first expeditions — but also gives you a better sense of who the major factions are, including the mysterious Lusks you fight.

Tutorials like this take a lot of time and are hard to make when aspects of Earthless can still change dramatically, which is why it wasn’t available in the Next Fest demo. We’ll be sure to share more on this when we can.

[hr][/hr]
The above isn’t a comprehensive list of everything we’re tracking, but it does represent the most common feedback we got. We’d love to still hear from you if you have something you’d like to add. We’re also elbow deep in discussions about what is next ahead of the Early Access launch — including more opportunities for you and your friends to play Earthless!

Thank you for taking the time to read this and be a part of this community. If you haven’t already, please join [url=https://discord.gg/mJu5ef6Y9E][b]our Discord[/b][/url] and [b][url=https://twitter.com/earthlessgame]follow us on Twitter[/url][/b] so you can stay up to date on everything.

Talk soon,

Steven

notes.title: Managing your crew in Earthless
notes.content:
[h3][i]Captain, it's time to solve a dilemma! We've recovered some Lusk technology and need to decided how to use it to benefit our ship. The Gunnery Officer thinks it should be used to elevate our weapons to the next level, but our Science Officer disagrees, saying that further research is needed before we make a rash decision...[/i][/h3]

[h3]In Earthless, a Captain is only as good as their crew. Manage your crew's relationships correctly and you'll  see wide-ranging benefits on the battle grid. Ignore their advice, and you'll face a range of negative debuffs. We sat down with Game Director, Hoi-Fung to explain crew management in more detail [/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/0a8283365a79ee1cc992fa68a07012313ae3e029.jpg[/img]

[b]How and when did the addition of a crew management mechanic enter Earthless' development?[/b]

From the very beginning, we wanted to create an experience that really evoked that feeling of being your own starship captain — the intrigue, the interpersonal drama, the impossible decisions. But the earliest prototypes of Earthless mostly focused on combat and exploration. In fact, we treated it like a D&D campaign, where we still had in person dungeon master-style narration for the events to the players.

As Earthless evolved and we were able to dig deeper into that idea of Captain Fantasy, it quickly became clear that a captain without a crew isn't much of a captain at all. So we started looking at ways we could incorporate a crew into the game and took a lot of inspiration from shows like Star Trek and Battlestar Galactica where the cast was often the officers on the bridge, each with their own unique worldview and speciality. It felt like a great fit for Earthless.

Over time the system grew more and more complex. Like any good roguelike, we saw an opportunity to generate a new crew for each voyage, with their own personality traits that would (hopefully) lead to some really fun interpersonal drama and conflict aboard your ship. This demo is only a taster for what’s to come!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/27c3cbddc51790c51f4b05bd117b689b0526d8ef.png[/img]

[b]How does the crew system work and how will it affect other game mechanics?[/b]

Now we're talking! So on each voyage you're assigned five officers who represent the basic functions of your ship: Gunnery Officer, Chief Engineer, Communications Officer, Navigation Officer, and Science Officer. These specialties are also reflected in the different "suits" of cards available. For example, a lot of damage-dealing cards are naturally Gunnery cards.

Each officer has personality traits that'll loosely define their perspective. And as you voyage deeper into space, they'll often weigh in with their perspective on what choices you should be making. For example, when landing on a narrative event, your crew all hops into a chat channel to discuss the event and vocalize their opinion (if they have one). 

Choices you make that align with a crew member's perspective will increase their morale, while going against their wishes decreases it. So it'll be up to you to decide how to manage your crew when they have opposing ideas on how to handle all the different situations you'll find yourself in.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/0dd8bf8789d78368708beac7686f23bbb357efe9.png[/img]

[b]If the player fails to maintain a good relationship with a crew member, are there any negative effects that they can expect to experience?[/b]

Oh, absolutely! Because each crew member specializes in a different function of your ship, you can expect that pissing them off is going to lead to some dire consequences. If your strategy primarily relies on dealing heavy damage, you might want to think twice before you upset your Gunnery Officer.

This is a system we see SO much potential in, so also expect it to grow throughout Early Access, too!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/f8f84a33f94bdec8f305fca9b200534e0549b288.jpg[/img]

[b]Any tips for how players can keep their crew in check?[/b]

A good leader knows it's impossible to appease everyone all the time. So don't be afraid to make choices just because one of your officers won't like it – especially if the outcome is worth the risk.

When push comes to shove, I always like to side with the officers who actually empower my ship and complement my combat strategies. With the rest, it's about mitigating and keeping them just happy enough to keep them from burning the ship down while I'm napping.

notes.title: Earthless Demo tips and tricks!
notes.content:
[h3]Attention all captains! We hope you're enjoying playing through the Steam Next Fest demo for Earthless! Travelling across the cosmos is no easy task though, and danger awaits any brave enough to try! To help you out in your search for a habitable planet, we've put together some tips and tricks.[/h3]

[h2]1. Use Your Ship's Predictive AI[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/cc05653b69324285832c0642529a2ded570e0911.png[/img]

The most powerful tool in your arsenal isn't a Tactical Strike card. It's your ship's Predictive AI module that displays what your enemies will do on their next turn. Press TAB to engage this feature, and you'll see blue lines displaying where enemy ships will move, whether they'll attack you, and how much damage those attacks will deal.

But wait! There's more!

The Predictive AI can be used to see how enemies will react to your actions. For example, when moving your ship on the grid, hold TAB before selecting a square to see how enemies will respond. The same goes for playing cards! Try selecting a basic Missile Launch and hovering your mouse over an enemy within range to see if their next move will change based on if you attack them.

PRO TIP: about to take some damage from a Lusk Grunt and don't have any Shields? Try attacking them instead! Many Lusk units have an ability to replenish their shields when depleted. Using the Predictive Ship AI, you can see if one is about to attack you. Try targeting it with an attack card and keep holding TAB to see if the incoming damage will force the Lusk unit to change to a defense manoeuvre instead.

[h2]2. Reduce, Reuse, Recycle[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/076de3198c45f03124bdf0f967cc180d01b593a7.png[/img]

Every time you complete three events / nodes on the Star Map, you unlock one of Earthless' most important — but easy to underestimate — features: recycling a card. This removes a card from your deck, which effectively increases your odds of drawing more important, powerful cards. You should be recycling as often as you can. 

The recycle menu can be found by entering the Manufacturing Screen (the wrench and screwdriver icon on the bottom left of your Command Console). An indicator will tell you how many events / Star Map nodes you have to complete before Recycling is available.

Deckbuilder veterans will know this well, but removing unwanted cards is vital to building an unstoppable deck. There's a lot of nuance on how to choose which cards to discard, but it's typically a safe choice to remove the basic Missile Launch and Shields Up cards as you earn more powerful attack and defense cards.

[h2]3. Be Careful Of Your Heat[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/4284f638ffbbb311fc393a44deae1b4cfa094517.png[/img]

Each time you move you generate Heat, and your ship can store a maximum of 4 Heat points. Once you're maxed out, you'll either need to end your turn or use a card like Vent Heat to reduce your Heat level so you can move again.

But be careful when running your engines hot. Acquiring more than 4 Heat will add Overheat cards to the top of your Draw Pile.

When you have an Overheat card in your hand, you'll take damage for every action you do until you spend 1 Energy to play that card. It can seriously disrupt your strategy, so always keep an eye on your heat and manage it effectively. This is especially important for the Clarke-class ship in the Next Fest demo, which has limited options for reducing Heat early on.

[h2]4. Don't Ignore your Artifacts and Upgrades[/h2]

Depending on where you venture in the Star Map, you're likely to start picking up some valuable resources that can either augment your cards or let you craft entirely new ones. Do not let them sit in your inventory. Use them. Artifacts let you augment cards, like increasing the range of Gunnery cards, and while it might be tempting to sit on an Artifact in hopes that you'll get a powerful card to make it even more powerful. But, more often than not, using an Artifact on whatever you have available is the better option (especially in the demo when you're only exploring one Star Map). Likewise, don't forget to spend your resources to craft Artifacts and cards from the schematics you might collect from Salvage Sites!

[h2]5. Be Wary of How Choices Will Affect Your Crew[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/0dd8bf8789d78368708beac7686f23bbb357efe9.png[/img]

As you venture further through the Star Map, you'll come across several difficult decisions and events that demand your attention. As the captain of your ship, it falls on you and no-one else to solve these dilemmas. Be careful to read them carefully and think about your decisions before picking. Each choice will improve relations with certain members of your crew and degrade relations with others. Every one onboard has their own opinions, after all! As you improve relations with each crew member, you'll receive certain bonuses. Be sure to manage these crew relationships properly, to maximise the benefits you receive in battle.

notes.title: Play the Earthess Next Fest demo now!
notes.content:
[h3]It's time for lift-off! Captain your crew and find a new home for humanity in the Earthless demo, available to play now as part of Steam Next Fest![/h3]

We spoke to our Game Director, Hoi-Fung about the demo and what players can expect to experience! Here's what he had to say.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/010ab7f4f68e458b43431673558b1064121ef9cf.png[/img]
[b]How would you describe Earthless to someone who's come across the demo in Steam Next Fest?[/b]

I think every sci-fi nerd has, at some point, wondered what it'd be like to be Captain Kirk and sit in that chair. How would you handle those tough decisions? Could you find that balance between completing your mission while also caring for your crew? That's Earthless. It's a game that strives to — at every level — evoke that fantasy of being a starship captain. And the roguelike genre lets you undergo these voyages where you never really know what to expect on each one. This is especially true regarding your crew, who have unique personalities that you'll have to constantly manage if you hope to make it to your destination.

For those who are super familiar with these genres, though, I'd say that Earthless is an elegant mix of different genres that defies simple descriptions. There's the roguelike deckbuilding that you know and love, but the grid-based combat adds a whole new dimension of strategy that makes Earthless feel very unique. And add to that your crew constantly chirping in your ear.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/27c3cbddc51790c51f4b05bd117b689b0526d8ef.png[/img]

[b]What advice would you give to players going for their first run in the demo?[/b]

Don't be afraid to take risks or make mistakes — especially in the beginning. It can be a lot of fun when things don't quite work out in your favor and even a bad voyage can still be a thrilling experience. More importantly, if you experiment and try new things you're more likely to stumble into strategies you might never have considered before!

Also, when building your deck, stick to just one or two general themes. Instead of always picking what seems like the strongest card at that moment, it's sometimes better to pick a weaker card that complements your other cards. 

Lastly, don’t forget to use the tab to preview your enemies turn! Understanding what they are going to do is absolutely critical to being a better player.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/0dd8bf8789d78368708beac7686f23bbb357efe9.png[/img]

[b]What can you tell us about the enemies players will be fighting in the demo, the Lusks?[/b]

So, the story in Earthless is something we're very excited about and I don't want to give too much away! We really wanted to have the first enemy to have a nautical feel to them. They aren’t sentient but are an integral part of the galaxy's ecosystem. Think of them like the immune system of the galaxy - a common retro-sci-fi inspired concept.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/0c626a275afed302736c6aee854bc9d4a2bbfe46.png[/img]

[b]How does the demo compare to the version of the game that will be available at the Early Access release?[/b]

Think of the demo like a little taste of what's to come when Earthless releases into Early Access in February 2024. You'll get a good grip of the basic systems, like combat, crafting, and crew management, and also get to experience several of the events like salvage sites, narrative encounters, and more. 

A full Earthless run will consist of 3 star maps with 3 bosses. The demo ends after the first starmap/boss so expect harder difficulty when Early Access is out! Not only that, we will start to tease more of the story as we get closer to launch. Things aren’t as simple as they seem….

Early Access launch (and beyond) will introduce even more cards, enemy types, factions, encounters, upgrades — just a plethora of content to explore.

[i]Blackbird Interactive[/i] and [i]Team17 Digital[/i] have today revealed the first look at gameplay for the upcoming, strategic sci-fi adventure , coming to Steam Early Access in early 2024. The new video explores the game’s core systems and dives into Earthless’ unique blend of grid-based exploration and tactical combat, intricate crew management and impactful trade-off choices, and expansive storytelling inspired by classic science fiction novels.

[h3]Key Features[/h3]

[list]
[*] [b]Captain on Deck:[/b] Captain a starship in daring roguelike voyages through webs of treacherous and ever-changing star systems to lead the survival of the species. Engage with enemies in tactical grid-based combat and make difficult decisions that could directly impact the well-being of your crew.
[*] [b]Play the Hand You’re Dealt:[/b] Collect over 75 cards (with more to come in future updates), each with unique abilities and tactical combinations. Build the perfect hand to boost your capabilities and steel your ship against mysterious, interstellar threats.

[*] [b]Bring A Friend:[/b] At early access launch, play with a friend in two-player co-op mode. Work together to discover unique cards and forge humanity’s new frontier together.

notes.title: Meet the Director Q&A!
notes.content:
[h3]We'd like to introduce you all to the game director on Earthless, Hoi-Fung Ma, who first pitched this project at Blackbird Interactive several years ago.[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/9e128baf1f81f821670c486da73f1a4fd7ed859e.png[/img]

[b]So how did Earthless first come to be? How did you get started on the project?[/b]

HOI-FUNG: I can’t believe that the original pitch for Earthless was almost four years ago already! Time really flies. I first started at BBI as a producer for Crossfire Legion and then Minecraft Legends, before having the opportunity to pitch Earthless (codenamed Project Owl) through BBI’s Skunkworks incubator program — alongside two other wonderful team members, Maher Manoubi and Youhan Guan.

[i]Note: the Skunkworks program, run about every year, allows anyone at BBI to team up and pitch a game idea that could become the studio's next original game. If the idea is chosen, the team gets a bonus and dedicated time and resources to take the project to the next phase (prototyping etc.). If the game isn't selected, the intellectual property rights revert back to the team — and they are free to make it on their own still or even take it elsewhere if they'd like. Hardspace: Shipbreaker was the first game to come out of this program.[/i]

HOI-FUNG: Going back to Earthless, the idea came when we started discussing our mutual love for deckbuilding board games and tactics games. We believed there was something special about combining the two genres, along with BBI's legacy of immersive sci-fi worldbuilding. We first started with a paper prototype, which got moved onto Tabletop Simulator once the Covid pandemic started and we couldn't meet in person. That really provided the base concept and potential, along with a pitch deck; then BBI met Team17 who loved what they saw and proper development of Earthless began!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/bbb2f202f786a6643b82faadd2188a790ab0c069.gif[/img]
[i]When the Covid pandemic hit, the Earthless team adapted their paper prototype to Tabletop Simulator so they could continue to workshop the idea remotely.[/i]

[b]What do you think Earthless does differently from other games in this genre?[/b]

HOI-FUNG: We believe that our dedication to immersing players in the captain fantasy — your emotional bond with your crew and your mission — is going to make Earthless something special. It's not just about collecting the right cards or getting that perfect run, but also about the stories that'll unfold on each new voyage.

The genre relies heavily on having players adapt to new situations and cards that are dealt each time they play; just like the captains in the classic sci-fi shows that we love (Star Trek, Battlestar Galactica etc.) have to face an ever-expanding array of surprising events and challenging situations with each new episode.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/291a26c0b6c81998beadbc36708572c562c643b3.gif[/img]

[b]What's been your favorite aspect of working on the game so far?[/b]

HOI-FUNG: The best part is undoubtedly working with such a passionate team to create something new and fresh. I see the evolution of Earthless each step of the way, and every day it gets better because the people that work on it really want to make the best game possible. There’s something electric about that work environment!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/3c3c055b62b92e26b7c2b8083add00e428cfc38c.gif[/img]

[b]What are you most excited for players to experience when Earthless launches next year?[/b]

HOI-FUNG: Oof, hard to pick just one thing! I’m definitely looking forward to the moment players start finding combos that even we didn’t know existed and post builds online. I can’t wait to see the community blossom as we get this in the hands of players and really start tuning the game with their feedback and input. That's why we are doing Early Access in the first place!

notes.title: A deep dive look at Blackbird Interactive and Team 17's new roguelike: Earthless
notes.content:
[h1]☀️ Outrun the Sun ☀️[/h1]

[i][h3]We thought we had billions of years before our Sun died. We were wrong.[/h3][/i]
[previewyoutube=N3--QLAW76I;full][/previewyoutube]
Now humanity is thrust into the cosmic winds in search of a new home, and it's up to you to get them there. In Earthless, you play as one of many different captains, exploring unique sectors of our galaxy to uncover a life-viable planet. Like any good roguelike, each voyage won't play out the same way twice. You'll face different compositions of enemies, obstacles, and — key to Earthless — narrative events with consequences that could save or doom you and your ship.

Making those decisions won't fall on you alone, however. With every new voyage, you'll be paired with a new crew of randomly-generated officers with their own personality and characteristics. Survival depends on how you manage these officers and their (often opposing) perspectives.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/4515b4077d9f806efd000ca0e6dc9098dfaf78d5.png[/img]
[b]FUN FACT[/b]

[i]Earthless' user interface is entirely diegetic, so you actually feel like a captain interacting with a computer console. You're not just playing cards, but feeding instruction chips into your ship's computer![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/d26861d3f9952ca3a54c2c540506b0574beda649.png[/img]
[h3]FEATURES DEEP DIVE[/h3]

[b]Play alone or co-op[/b]
It can get lonely out in the deep black of space, so why not bring a friend? In co-op mode, each player controls their own ship during combat and will face much tougher encounters. Communication and strategy will be key as both of your turns will happen simultaneously. That opens up a whole new world of strategy where you can coordinate playing different cards to really maximize their benefit.

[b]Intense Tactical Combat[/b]
Grid-based combat adds another strategic layer to the encounters. How you move and position your ship is just as important as what cards you play. Obstacles and space terrain might block your attacks or force you into a deadly corner. And not every encounter needs to end in bloodshed, either.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/aa5c1753d67bd6907f4c36c82d54e72ff14fccf0.png[/img]

[b]Treacherous Ever-changing Galaxy[/b]
Each new voyage is a new story waiting to be told. You'll fight through different combat encounters, narrative events, crew dilemmas, and discover new cards. The game will evolve through Steam Early Access with future updates including new ships to pilot, new cards, additional enemy factions, events, regions to explore, and more.

[b]Immersive Sci-fi Adventure[/b]
One thing that differentiates Earthless from other roguelike deckbuilders is its emphasis on storytelling — both in the personal stories that'll unfold between you and your crew based on your decisions, as well as the wider narrative of humanity diving deeper into the cosmos. Everything in Earthless is designed to make you feel as if you're truly sitting in the captain's chair.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44238279/077c6786477c4dcc368b20265ba41689f9a18edf.gif[/img]
[h3]TL;DR[/h3]
[list]
[*] Earthless is a grid-based tactics and deckbuilding roguelike.
[*] It will be coming to Steam Early Access in 2024.
[*] Combat plays out on a tactical grid where positioning and cover are key to survival.
[*] Each voyage pairs you with a randomized crew who oversee different aspects of your ship.
[*] Manage their morale to unlock powerful bonuses, or upset them at your peril.
[*] Play alone or with a friend in two-player co-op.
[*] Regular updates will add new cards, factions, story, and much more.
[/list]
[i]If you'd like to go deeper and learn more about Earthless, check out this interview with [url=https://www.pcgamer.com/earthless-is-a-new-sci-fi-deck-builder-from-the-creators-of-homeworld-3-where-youll-need-to-come-up-with-ludicrous-game-breaking-combos-and-win-over-your-crew-to-have-a-chance-at-saving-humanity/]PC Gamer[/url] or find out more about our approach to Early Access on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2058960/Earthless/]our Steam page[/url].[/i]

[h2]Wishlist Earthless now![/h2]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2058960/Earthless/

notes.content:
Okay, so you're not being chased by an army of murderous robots that are only seconds behind you, but you're still jumping around trying to find a new home for the last of humanity who managed to escape a doomed planet. Earthless is a roguelike deckbuilder from Blackbird Interactive, although you wouldn't know it from the cinematic teaser trailer shown at the PC Gaming Show tonight, which was heavy on the dramatic yet hopeful voiceover. As the captain of the fleet, your job is to lead everyone to a safe harbour.

notes.title: Earthless arrives in Steam Early Access in 2024!
notes.content:
[h2]Humanity’s fate rests in your hands, Captains. We may have lost our home, but humanity will chart a new course amongst the stars! 🌌[/h2]

[previewyoutube=N3--QLAW76I;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Team17 and Blackbird Interactive join forces for brand new sci-fi roguelike deckbuilder, [i]Earthless[/i].[/b]

In [i]Earthless[/i], players will experience a rich, sci-fi story of loss, hope, and human endurance following the destruction of the Sun. You will captain humanity’s final colony ships through space in a series of roguelike adventures, exploring a web of ever-changing and treacherous star systems while engaging in strategic, grid-based combat with mysterious, interstellar enemies.

During each voyage, you will also build a deck of unique tactical abilities and manage the crew on board your vessel, making difficult ethical decisions that could directly impact the well-being of their team…and the survival of humanity.

[h3]KEY FEATURES[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Captain on Deck:[/b] Captain a starship in daring roguelike voyages through webs of treacherous and ever-changing star systems to lead the survival of the species. Engage with enemies in tactical grid-based combat and make difficult decisions that could directly impact the well-being of your crew.
[*] [b]Play the Hand You’re Dealt:[/b] Collect 50+ cards, each with unique abilities and tactical combinations. Build the perfect hand to boost your capabilities and steel your ship against mysterious, interstellar threats.
[*] [b]Win Their Hearts:[/b] With each new voyage comes a brand-new crew! Win their allegiance to unlock powerful bonuses, or disregard their needs at your own peril.
[*] [b]Bring A Friend:[/b] At early access launch, play with a friend in two-player co-op mode. Work together to discover unique cards and forge humanity’s new frontier together.
[/list]

Find out more: https://www.earthlessgame.com/
